solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One despicable sort in film about buccaneers

indicators.note: the one and the despicable sort are placed in the film, so the word signals containment

parts.note: PIC is short for picture, a film
one is the Roman numeral I
a rat is a despicable person

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a nasty character appearing in a pirate movie.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means relating to or characteristic of pirates, and buccaneers were seafaring raiders.

clue.text: Rise of right political party in part of W Yorks

indicators.note: in a down clue rise means read upwards, from the bottom

parts.note: yes, as in 'right!', expresses agreement
the DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A right-wing party gaining ground in a Yorkshire district.
explanation.definitionFit: Pudsey is a town in West Yorkshire, between Leeds and Bradford.

clue.text: Cheese stuffed into apricot tart

indicators.note: the cheese is packed inside the words apricot tart

explanation.surface: A dessert recipe: a fruit tart filled with cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Ricotta is a soft white Italian whey cheese, often used in tarts.

clue.text: Don threw a wobbly in Educating Rita, perhaps

indicators.note: throwing a wobbly is a tantrum; wobbly also says the letters of don threw a are unsteady

explanation.surface: An academic loses his temper in the play Educating Rita.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don' is a university tutor, as in the play, but is only letters here. A wobbly is British slang for a tantrum.
explanation.definitionFit: Willy Russell's Educating Rita has just two characters, the tutor Frank and Rita, so it is an example of a two-person play.

clue.text: Health worker's daily information on source of funding cut at source

parts.note: a daily, or char, is a cleaning woman who comes in daily
gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: the word loses its first letter, its source

parts.note: a purse is a source of money

explanation.surface: A health worker's daily briefing about funding cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'daily' is not a newspaper but a British cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior nurse in charge of a hospital ward is a medical professional.

clue.text: Ancient queen endlessly patient during Spanish dance

indicators.note: the shortened patient falls in the middle of the dance, as if happening during it

parts.note: the jota is a lively folk dance from Aragon in Spain

indicators.note: endlessly says the word for patient loses its final letter

parts.note: a doctor's patient is a case

explanation.surface: Pictures an old queen, short on patience, at a Spanish dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops the last letter of the word for patient; 'during' then sets what remains inside the Aragonese folk dance.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend she was queen of Thebes, mother and wife of Oedipus.

clue.text: Jack, old English man's name

parts.note: J is jack in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: Jack is an old English name for a man.
explanation.definitionFit: Joe is a common male first name.

clue.text: A pain in the neck contracted when twisting around

indicators.note: twisting turns the whole string round to read the other way
contracted means the word is shortened by its last letter

parts.note: a crick is a painful stiffness in the neck

explanation.surface: Twisting one's head gives a stiff neck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contracted' cuts CRICK to CRIC; A then CRIC, reversed by 'when twisting'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin preposition is used before dates to mean approximately.

clue.text: A US tram adapted for island

indicators.note: adapted means the letters of a US tram are rearranged

explanation.surface: An American tram converted for use on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumatra is a large island of Indonesia.

clue.text: A form of diplomacy verbally criticised

indicators.note: verbally means the phrase for a form of diplomacy is spoken

parts.note: tact is a form of diplomacy, so 'a tact'

explanation.surface: Diplomats criticised in words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'verbally' looks like part of the definition, 'criticised in words', but it signals the sound.
explanation.definitionFit: To attack someone in speech or print is to criticise them severely.

clue.text: Head of department takes more than half a month to judge academic qualification

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
only four of the month's seven letters are kept, a little over half

parts.note: October is a month
to rate is to judge or assess

explanation.surface: A department head spends weeks marking a doctoral thesis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'more than half a month' keeps OCTO, the first four of OCTOBER's seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctorate is the highest university degree, such as a PhD.

clue.text: What occurs when dreaming? It's brief

parts.note: REM, rapid eye movement, is the phase of sleep in which dreams happen

explanation.surface: A question about dreams, then a curt reply that it is short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' is a noun here: one's terms of reference.
explanation.definitionFit: A remit is the scope of a task given to someone, the same as their brief.

clue.text: Old time artist, no star

parts.note: ex- means former, old
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A painter of yesteryear who never became famous.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra in a film is a background performer, the opposite of the lead actor.

clue.text: Involved in bar work, say, we hear James can sit around

indicators.note: says the short form of the name is to be taken by its sound

parts.note: Jim is the familiar form of James

indicators.note: around means the letters of the phrase can sit are moved about

explanation.surface: Someone called James can lounge about in a pub, doing bar work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' is the gymnast's apparatus, not a pub counter.
explanation.definitionFit: Bars, parallel or asymmetric, are apparatus in gymnastics, so work on them is athletic exercise.

clue.text: Cabinet member's brief time in several dramatic episodes?

definitions.note: possessive here works as the adjective, of a minister

parts.note: mini means small or short

indicators.note: time goes in the episodes

parts.note: a serial is a drama in instalments

explanation.surface: A minister's short stint in a run of dramatic events.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means relating to a government minister, a member of cabinet.

clue.text: Time to spend at home and learn veggie cooking

indicators.note: cooking suggests the letters of and learn veggie are mixed and worked up

explanation.surface: Using spare time at home to learn vegetarian cookery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'veggie' hints at a garden, but both it and 'learn' are just letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This British term is the period an employee leaving a job is paid to stay at home, kept away from work.

clue.text: Sets about last character, American with a new revolver

indicators.note: sets goes about the last letter

parts.note: to lay is to set, as a table
Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: An American with a new gun prepares for the final showdown.
explanation.definitionFit: A lazy Susan is a rotating tray on a table, something that revolves.

clue.text: Least robust rose ultimately withers if drenched?

indicators.note: if drenched pictures the other pieces surrounded by wetness, so if signals containment

parts.note: drenched means wet

indicators.note: ultimately takes the last letter of rose

parts.note: a plant that withers dies

explanation.surface: A rose wilts if overwatered: the feeblest of plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rose' looks like the flower or a verb, but only its last letter counts; 'if drenched' is read as being soaked through, so surrounded by wetness.
explanation.definitionFit: Weedy means thin and feeble, so the superlative is the feeblest of all.

clue.text: Key award announced, backed by unknown individual in industrial area

indicators.note: backed by puts the following pieces after it, supporting it

parts.note: Enter is a key on a computer keyboard

indicators.note: announced means the word for award is taken as spoken

parts.note: a prize is an award
Z is an unknown quantity in algebra
one means a single individual

explanation.surface: A key award is announced, supported by an anonymous person.
explanation.walkthrough: PRISE has the sound of PRIZE.
explanation.definitionFit: Such zones are areas given tax breaks and eased planning to attract industry and business.

clue.text: Office worker, given curry, oddly rejected a fried dish

parts.note: a temp is a temporary office worker

indicators.note: the odd letters of curry are thrown out, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: An office worker turns down a curry for a fried meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempura is a Japanese dish of seafood or vegetables fried in light batter.

clue.text: Resort is hot and fairly pleasant

parts.note: Nice is a resort on the French Riviera

explanation.surface: A holiday spot is hot and quite agreeable.
explanation.definitionFit: Adding -ish to an adjective softens it, so this means reasonably agreeable.

clue.text: Top man wearing a piece of jewellery

indicators.note: the jewellery is worn by, so wrapped round, the man

parts.note: a bead is a small piece of jewellery
he is a man

explanation.surface: A senior man sporting a jewel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' is a verb: to cut the top off.
explanation.definitionFit: To top someone is slang for kill, and to behead is to cut off the head.

clue.text: Block a view of ancient city

parts.note: to dam is to block
a scene is a view

explanation.surface: Someone obstructs the view of an old city.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means relating to Damascus, one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities.

clue.text: Musician turned us against piano exercises

indicators.note: against means next to, set beside the following pieces
turned means the word us is read backwards

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
PE is physical education, exercises

explanation.surface: A pianist turned against us by endless practice.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz von Suppé was an Austrian composer of operettas and overtures, such as Light Cavalry.

clue.text: Money from abroad — firm needs constant investment

indicators.note: investment is read as putting one thing inside another, as in clothing

parts.note: sure means firm or certain
C is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light

explanation.surface: A company needs steady investment of foreign cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'investment' plays on its old sense of clothing: C is invested in SURE.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the currency of Ecuador until the US dollar replaced it in 2000.

clue.text: Supply on-line joke?

parts.note: E is the prefix for electronic or online, as in email
a quip is a joke

explanation.surface: Asks whether a joke can be found online.
explanation.definitionFit: To equip is to provide with what is needed, to supply.

clue.text: Lock keeper sports hat in heat? Not half

indicators.note: the two pieces are placed in the shortened heat
not half means half of the word heat is dropped

parts.note: to sport is to show off, to put on airs
lid is slang for a hat

explanation.surface: A canal lock-keeper wearing a hat in hot weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lock keeper' suggests a canal, but the lock is a lock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A hair slide is a clip that holds a lock of hair in place.

clue.text: Old Man's place: house close to Torquay

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: An old man's home near Torquay, a Devon seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: The Old Man of Hoy is a famous sea stack in Orkney.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orkney island is where the sea stack called the Old Man stands.

clue.text: Two tracks together making pattern

parts.note: to trace is to track, a footprint trail
RY, railway, is the second track

explanation.surface: Two lines of footprints meet and form a design.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two tracks together' gives two pieces: TRACE (to track) and RY (railway, a railway track).
explanation.definitionFit: Tracery is ornamental interlaced work, as in Gothic window stonework, so a decorative pattern.

clue.text: Scoffed when guided round a Spanish church

indicators.note: guided goes round the other pieces

parts.note: led means guided
un is Spanish for a

explanation.surface: Someone sneered while being taken round a church in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoff is informal for eating greedily, so it can stand for having had a midday meal.
